explanation: Toggle a character in a set on each occurrence. The set contains precisely the characters with odd frequency. A palindrome permutation exists if at most one character has odd frequency.
timeComplexity: O(n) expected time. Each character updates one expected-constant-time hash entry.
spaceComplexity: O(u) auxiliary space for u distinct characters. At most u distinct characters have parity/count state.
attribution: Unmodified reference source: epi_judge_cpp_solutions/is_string_permutable_to_palindrome.cc. Elements of Programming Interviews Judge authors; repository LICENSE: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives 4.0 International. Explanation authored for EPI Practice.
correctness: Mirrored positions in a palindrome consume characters in pairs, leaving at most one unpaired middle character. The toggle set contains exactly the characters with odd counts, so size at most one is both necessary and sufficient.
walkthrough: For "bbcaac", b, c and a each occur twice. Every toggle is canceled, leaving the odd-count set empty; a permutation such as "abccba" is palindromic, so return true.
edgeCases: An empty string passes with no odd counts.
Two or more odd-frequency characters fail.
